item.title: Iranian vessel in Hormuz hit, while Houthis expand control of shipping lane
item.description: The Iran-backed Houthis expanded their control over the strategy Bab-el-Mandeb strait, as strikes continued in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: After years of red tape, 9/11 Pentagon Memorial visitor education center breaks ground
item.description: A new visitor education center broke ground on Saturday at the National 9/11 Pentagon Memorial. The memorial honors the 184 people who died in the Sept. 11, 2001, attack on the Pentagon. Nikole Killion has more details about the center, set to open in 2029.

item.title: Police departments work to "change the culture" by building relationships with underprivileged kids
item.description: A nonprofit charity, in partnership with police departments, called Do the Right Thing honors the good works of students across the U.S. The Palm Springs chapter awarded 95 scholarships, helping underprivileged students achieve their dreams. Barry Petersen has the story.

item.title: Lithuania prepares for war, reinforcing its border against Russian tanks
item.description: On the edge of NATO territory in the Baltics, there is growing concern about the threat Russia poses. Aaron MacLean visited the capital of Lithuania to see how they're preparing.

item.title: El Niño weather pattern threatening West Coast beaches, homes
item.description: Communities across the West Coast braced for big, El Niño-powered storms this weekend. Andrew Kozak has the forecast and Jonathan Vigliotti reports from Dana Point, California, where there's a race to save beaches and homes.

item.title: U.S. military on high alert as Iran, allies target energy supply
item.description: Tom Hanson reports from the USS George Washington, deployed in the Middle East. All 50,000 U.S. personnel in the region are prepped for battle at any moment.

item.title: Trump visits Ireland amid skyrocketing energy prices
item.description: Americans are feeling the squeeze from skyrocketing fuel prices, with gas rising 16 cents from a week ago to a nationwide average of $4.31 per gallon. Concerns about oil prices followed President Trump during his trip to Ireland this weekend. Nancy Cordes has more details.

item.title: Trump brushes off AI fears: "Whoever wins AI wins"
item.description: President Trump brushed off the risks of artificial intelligence and warnings that the technology has gone rogue. The calls for caution were amplified by tech CEOs who say AI is advancing too fast. Ramy Inocencio has more.

item.title: How a wounded Air Force officer stayed safe in Iran after plane was shot down
item.description: Bravo, the code name for the Air Force officer shot down over Iran, survived for 48 hours on the ground with a broken back, broken arm and broken shoulder.

item.title: Paid brokers tout ties to Trump's orbit to lobby for presidential pardons
item.description: President Trump has developed his own vetting system for pardons.

item.title: Rams coach McVay says he almost left Rams because of insecurities
item.description: Sean McVay has become a generational talent, pacing toward the best ever, in the decade since the Rams hired him as head coach. But McVay says he almost left the Rams because of his insecurities.

item.title: Even with Rams a Super Bowl favorite, coach Sean McVay is "tormented"
item.description: With the Rams a Super Bowl favorite as the season kicks off, coach Sean McVay is forging ahead, having learned from past successes and failures.

item.description: "60 Minutes" airs Sundays at 7 p.m. ET/PT

item.title: Pardon brokers offer to "put pressure on the president" — at sky-high costs
item.description: Hidden cameras captured lobbyists as they tried to woo a potential client interested in obtaining a pardon from President Trump.

item.title: 6 takeaways from our interview with the officer shot down in Iran
item.description: In his first interview, Bravo, an Air Force colonel who was shot down in Iran, told 60 Minutes his story of survival and provided new details about the rescue operation.

item.title: Watch: Videos show rescue of downed Air Force officers 2 days apart
item.description: Dramatic video, obtained first by 60 Minutes, shows the rescue of two Air Force officers shot down over a mountainous desert region of Iran back in April.

item.title: Air Force officer prayed while "free-falling" after being shot down in Iran
item.description: Badly wounded and alone in Iran's desert, downed U.S. Air Force officer Dude 44 Bravo evaded capture for days as the Iranian forces and the U.S. military searched for him.

item.title: Extended Interview: Air Force officer shot down in Iran on surviving behind enemy lines
item.description: In an extended interview with 60 Minutes correspondent Norah O'Donnell, Bravo, an Air Force colonel, provided new details about his fight to survive behind enemy lines in Iran, and the rescue operation that brought him and crewmate Alpha back home.

item.title: U.S. Air Force officer shot down in Iran says it's a "modern-day miracle" he survived | 60 Minutes
item.description: Dude 44 Bravo was part of a two-man U.S. Air Force crew shot down over Iran in April. He describes a terrifying ejection, how he evaded Iranian forces for two days, and what he said to his rescuers.

item.title: Ross Douthat says "no story looms larger" than the latest AI developments | 60 Minutes
item.description: New correspondent Ross Douthat says "no story looms larger than the latest developments in artificial intelligence." The technology and its impacts will be a major focus of 60 Minutes reporting.

item.title: The McVay way: Coaching the Los Angeles Rams while handling heavy expectations | 60 Minutes
item.description: Sean McVay has become a generational talent, pacing toward the best ever, in the decade since the Rams hired him as head coach. But McVay says he almost left the Rams because of his insecurities.

item.description: Hidden cameras captured lobbyists as they tried to woo a potential client expressing interest in a pardon from President Trump.

item.title: 9/13/2026: Shot Down Over Iran, The Pardon Economy, Battering Ram
item.description: First, U.S. Air Force officer shot down in Iran says it's a "modern-day miracle" he survived. Then, brokers are offering felons a path to Trump pardons — at a steep price with no guarantees. And, McVay, Stafford on Rams culture.

item.title: 9/13: CBS Weekend News
item.description: President Trump pushes back against the new AI warnings; Trump visits Ireland amid skyrocketing energy prices.

item.title: U.S. wins fifth straight women's FIBA World Cup, beating France 97-79
item.description: Despite the final score, this one wasn't easy; the Americans faced their biggest deficit in the tournament in a long time.

item.title: Missile crisis: The hard truths about America's military arsenal
item.description: In the early days of the war against Iran, the U.S. fired off thousands of long-range, precision-guided missiles. Now, with a depleted arsenal, the Pentagon seeks to replenish its stockpiles, an effort that will cost billions and take years.

item.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei: "For too long the industry lied" about AI risks
item.description: The head of the artificial intelligence company calls the exponential rate of AI developments a "warning sign," with risks for humanity, and says, "We need to slow down." He talks with "Sunday Morning" about possible steps forward.

item.title: 2026 midterm election races to watch
item.description: CBS News has identified nine key Senate and 42 House races that will likely decide the majority — all of which can change during the midterm campaign.

item.title: Search underway for 130 people after Indonesian passenger ship overturns
item.description: Indonesian rescuers launched a search operation after authorities lost contact with a passenger ship carrying more than 240 people in the Java Sea.

item.title: Elena Rybakina wins U.S. Open over defending champ Aryna Sabalenka
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka, the two-time defending U.S. Open champion, was dethroned Saturday, losing to Elena Rybakina in three sets.
